Ben / Marissa — quick triage notes after 30m of logs & trace pulls:

Findings:
- Route-level backlog observed: requests for ACME are piling in the fronting queue (avg queue length spiked ~x25 on one worker pool).
- Concurrency cap on that model variant is at 24 per instance; during the spike we hit instance-level caps which cause requests to queue rather than fail-fast.
- Backpressure policies are configured to avoid overload by queuing; however, KV cache misses (their traffic profile includes many unique prefixes) amplify per-request work and lengthen service time.
- Error mode: transient 503s correlate with queue timeouts (time queued > service timeout). Not seeing OOMs or GPU crashes.

Immediate mitigations (recommendation):
1) Temporary increase concurrency cap to 36 on the affected pool (low risk, small latency cost).
2) Short-term routing: route ACME traffic to a variant with higher concurrency / lower per-request memory (quantized variant) for 2–4 hours.
3) Enable aggressive prefix KV caching for their hot prefixes (requires config change but can be same-day).
4) If we can't increase concurrency quickly, set a short 3s queue timeout to fail-fast and rely on client retries (avoid long queuing causing errors downstream).

I can enact (1) and (2) within 20–30 mins if we get approval for an emergency burst on Dedicated capacity or permission to adjust pool config for hosted. Need confirmation from ops to bump caps and from Marissa to coordinate messaging.

Attachments: small log snippet (prod-cluster-logs-snippet.txt)

—Vivek
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime
